paragraphs: Ativion sells software that K-12 school districts use to filter what students can reach online and to watch for signs that a student is at risk. The StudentKeeper side of the product handles classroom management and digital safety together, reporting into one place.

Filtering under the ContentKeeper name runs partly on district hardware and partly in the cloud, with one console covering both. Because it filters at the network layer, it reaches district-managed endpoints, personal devices, guest access and connected equipment alike. Districts can run it in the cloud, on premises, or as a mix, and set rules down to the level of individual sites.

The company says it has been in technology since 2002, serving education and enterprise customers with remote access and security products as well. Its lineup came together through acquisitions that included Netop and ContentKeeper, and the Ativion name itself dates to a 2024 rebrand.
